There's no code here to look at, so this is the general answer.

By default, React re-renders every child whenever its parent re-renders. It doesn't check if the props actually changed.

The fix is to wrap the child in `React.memo`. That tells React: skip this one if the props are the same as last time.

But there's a catch. If you pass a function or an object as a prop, a new one gets built on every render. It looks the same to you, but React sees a different value. So things like `onClick={() => doThing()}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}` will always count as "changed," even with `React.memo` in place.

To fix that, keep the function stable with `useCallback`, and the object stable with `useMemo`. Then the same value gets passed each time, and `React.memo` can actually do its job.
